_about: The priests side by side (plan 7.6b): wordings of priests and priesthood that more than one book shares, from Aaron and the Levites to the prophets, the psalms, Hebrews, Peter and Revelation, with what is alike and what differs. Every quotation machine-checked against the Berean; rows chosen and drafted by Claude Opus from the passages the theme map cites, the Berean editors' quotation notes and a search of the whole Berean; widened by the completeness search; every Alike and Different line read by the nine-reader panel (Sonnet). Takes no interpretive stance. A cell [verse, words, "aside"] is off the subject and shown, with an asterisk, for its shared words.
columns_note: The Law & history: Genesis to Esther. Psalms & wisdom: Job to the Song of Solomon. The Prophets: Isaiah to Malachi.

rows.title: Stand before the LORD to minister to Him

The Law & history: to stand before the LORD to serve Him
to stand and minister in His name for all time
like all his fellow Levites who stand there before the LORD
approach the altar to minister in the Holy Place
enters the Tent of Meeting to minister in the Holy Place
approach the altar to minister by presenting a food offering to the LORD
to stand before the congregation to minister to them
the priests could not stand there to minister because of the cloud
to minister before the ark of the LORD
to minister there regularly according to the daily requirements
the priests could not stand there to minister because of the cloud
to minister before the priests according to the daily requirement
the priests who minister to the LORD are sons of Aaron
the LORD has chosen you to stand before Him, to serve Him, to minister before Him
the priests who minister in the house of our God
Psalms & wisdom: all you servants of the LORD who serve by night in the house of the LORD
who stand in the house of the LORD
The Prophets: the foreigners who join themselves to the LORD to minister to Him
the Levites who minister before Me
the only Levites who may approach the LORD to minister before Him
who approach Me to minister before Me
stand before them to minister to them
are to approach Me to minister before Me. They will stand before Me to offer Me fat and blood
draw near to My table to minister before Me
who draw near to minister before the LORD
the priests are in mourning, those who minister before the LORD
Let the priests who minister before the LORD weep between the portico and the altar
Gospels & Acts: he was serving as priest before God
They had followed Jesus from Galilee to minister to Him
The letters: who ministers in the sanctuary and true tabernacle set up by the Lord, not by man

Revelation: they are before the throne of God and serve Him day and night in His temple

rows.alike: Many speak of the priests or Levites standing and ministering: "to stand before the LORD to serve Him" (Deuteronomy 10:8), "the Levites who minister before Me" (Jeremiah 33:22), "the priests who minister before the LORD" (Joel 2:17), and "every priest stands to minister" (Hebrews 10:11).
rows.different: Numbers 16:9 and Ezekiel 44:11 have "stand before the congregation to minister to them" and "stand before them to minister to them"; Isaiah 56:6 says it of "the foreigners who join themselves to the LORD"; Psalm 134:1 of "servants of the LORD who serve by night in the house of the LORD". Luke 1:8 has Zechariah "serving as priest before God"; Hebrews 8:2 speaks of one "who ministers in the sanctuary and true tabernacle set up by the Lord, not by man"; Revelation 7:15 of those "before the throne of God" who "serve Him day and night in His temple". In 1 Kings 8:11 and 2 Chronicles 5:14 "the priests could not stand there to minister because of the cloud".

rows.title: To pronounce blessings in His name

The Law & history: to pronounce blessings in His name
to serve Him and pronounce blessings in His name
to pronounce blessings in His name forever
the priests and the Levites stood to bless the people, and God heard their voice
he blessed the people in the name of the LORD of Hosts
he blessed the people in the name of the LORD
Psalms & wisdom: From the house of the LORD we bless you.
we bless you in the name of the LORD

rows.alike: Levi and the descendants of Aaron are set apart "to pronounce blessings in His name" (Deuteronomy 10:8; 1 Chronicles 23:13), and in 2 Chronicles 30:27 "the priests and the Levites stood to bless the people".
rows.different: In 2 Samuel 6:18 and 1 Chronicles 16:2 it is David who "blessed the people in the name of the LORD", "When David had finished sacrificing the burnt offerings and peace offerings". 2 Chronicles 30:27 adds "God heard their voice"; Psalm 118:26 says "From the house of the LORD we bless you"; Psalm 129:8 has "May none who pass by say to them" "we bless you in the name of the LORD".

rows.title: The lips of a priest: teaching the law

The Law & history: so that you may teach the Israelites all the statutes that the LORD has given them through Moses
He will teach Your ordinances to Jacob and Your law to Israel
Send back one of the priests you carried off from Samaria
he began to teach them how they should worship the LORD
without a priest to instruct them, and without the law
They taught throughout Judah, taking with them the Book of the Law of the LORD
the Levites who taught all Israel
to teach its statutes and ordinances in Israel
instructed the people in the Law as they stood in their places
Ezra the priest and scribe, and the Levites who were instructing the people
The Prophets: the law will never be lost to the priest
instruction from the priests will perish
Because you have rejected knowledge, I will also reject you as My priests
her priests teach for a price
Ask the priests for a ruling.
True instruction was in his mouth, and nothing false was found on his lips
For the lips of a priest should preserve knowledge, and people should seek instruction from his mouth, because he is the messenger of the LORD of Hosts
your instruction has caused many to stumble

rows.alike: The priests and Levites "teach" and "instruct": "He will teach Your ordinances to Jacob and Your law to Israel" (Deuteronomy 33:10), "the Levites who taught all Israel" (2 Chronicles 35:3), "people should seek instruction from his mouth" (Malachi 2:7).
rows.different: The Law and the histories give it as a charge or a record ("so that you may teach the Israelites all the statutes"; "They taught throughout Judah"); several prophets speak of it failing: "her priests teach for a price" (Micah 3:11), "instruction from the priests will perish" (Ezekiel 7:26), "your instruction has caused many to stumble" (Malachi 2:8). 2 Chronicles 15:3 recalls years "without a priest to instruct them, and without the law"; Malachi 2:7 calls the priest "the messenger of the LORD of Hosts".

rows.title: Distinguish between the holy and the common

The Law & history: You must distinguish between the holy and the common, between the clean and the unclean
You must distinguish between the unclean and the clean
You are therefore to distinguish between clean and unclean animals and birds
The Prophets: Her priests do violence to My law and profane My holy things. They make no distinction between the holy and the common, and they fail to distinguish between the clean and the unclean
They are to teach My people the difference between the holy and the common and show them how to discern between the clean and the unclean

rows.alike: Leviticus 10:10 and Ezekiel 44:23 pair "the holy and the common" with "the clean and the unclean", and Ezekiel 22:26 has both pairs again.
rows.different: Leviticus 10:10 has "You must distinguish"; Ezekiel 22:26 says "Her priests do violence to My law" and "They make no distinction"; Ezekiel 44:23 adds "teach My people". Leviticus 11:47 and 20:25 use the words of "animals".

rows.title: A ruling in every dispute

The Law & history: You are to go to the Levitical priests and to the judge who presides at that time
before the priests and judges who are in office at that time
to give a ruling in every dispute and case of assault
some of the Levites, priests, and heads of the Israelite families to judge on behalf of the LORD and to settle disputes
The Prophets: In any dispute, they shall officiate as judges and judge according to My ordinances

rows.alike: Deuteronomy 21:5 gives the priests "a ruling in every dispute"; 2 Chronicles 19:8 sets some of "the Levites, priests, and heads of the Israelite families" "to settle disputes"; and Ezekiel 44:24 says "In any dispute, they shall officiate as judges".
rows.different: Deuteronomy 17:9 and 19:17 name "the judge" or "judges" beside the priests, and 2 Chronicles 19:8 "heads of the Israelite families"; in Ezekiel 44:24 "they" themselves "officiate as judges" and "judge according to My ordinances".

rows.title: A priest must not defile himself for the dead

The Law & history: a priest is not to defile himself for a dead person among his people
except for his immediate family-his mother, father, son, daughter, or brother
or his unmarried sister who is near to him
He must not go near any dead body; he must not defile himself, even for his father or mother
Even if his father or mother or brother or sister should die, he is not to defile himself, because the symbol of consecration to his God is upon his head
The Prophets: A priest must not defile himself by going near a dead person. However, for a father, a mother, a son, a daughter, a brother, or an unmarried sister, he may do so
after he is cleansed, he must count off seven days for himself
he would not defile himself with the king's food or wine

rows.alike: "a priest is not to defile himself for a dead person" (Leviticus 21:1) and "A priest must not defile himself by going near a dead person" (Ezekiel 44:25), each except for close family, down to "an unmarried sister" (Ezekiel 44:25; "his unmarried sister", Leviticus 21:3).
rows.different: Leviticus 21:11 allows no exception: "even for his father or mother"; Ezekiel 44:26 adds "he must count off seven days for himself". Numbers 6:7 uses the words of another, "because the symbol of consecration to his God is upon his head", and Daniel 1:8 of "the king's food or wine".

rows.title: Whom a priest may marry

The Law & history: A priest must not marry a woman defiled by prostitution or divorced by her husband, for the priest is holy to his God
The woman he marries must be a virgin.
He is not to marry a widow, a divorced woman, or one defiled by prostitution. He is to marry a virgin from his own people
The Prophets: they shall not marry a widow or a divorced woman, but must marry a virgin of the descendants of the house of Israel, or a widow of a priest
Gospels & Acts: he who marries a divorced woman commits adultery
he who marries a divorced woman commits adultery

rows.alike: Leviticus 21:14 has "not to marry a widow, a divorced woman" and "marry a virgin"; Ezekiel 44:22 "not marry a widow or a divorced woman, but must marry a virgin".
rows.different: Leviticus 21:14 says "a virgin from his own people"; Ezekiel 44:22 says "a virgin of the descendants of the house of Israel, or a widow of a priest". Leviticus 21:7 gives the reason "for the priest is holy to his God". Matthew 5:32 and Luke 16:18 use "marries a divorced woman" of another matter.

rows.title: No wine when he enters

The Law & history: You and your sons are not to drink wine or strong drink when you enter the Tent of Meeting, or else you will die

be careful not to drink wine or strong drink

You ate no bread and drank no wine or strong drink
I have not had any wine or strong drink
Psalms & wisdom: it is not for kings to drink wine, or for rulers to crave strong drink
The Prophets: No priest may drink wine before he enters the inner court.
He commanded his sons not to drink wine
Gospels & Acts: He shall never take wine or strong drink

rows.alike: "not to drink wine or strong drink when you enter the Tent of Meeting" (Leviticus 10:9) and "No priest may drink wine before he enters the inner court" (Ezekiel 44:21).
rows.different: Leviticus 10:9 adds "or else you will die" and names "strong drink"; Ezekiel 44:21 names only "wine". The asides use the words of others: "You ate no bread and drank no wine or strong drink" (Deuteronomy 29:6), "the boy will be a Nazirite to God" (Judges 13:7), Hannah's "I have not had any wine or strong drink" (1 Samuel 1:15), "kings" (Proverbs 31:4), "Jonadab son of Rechab" (Jeremiah 35:6, 14), and one who "will be great in the sight of the Lord" (Luke 1:15).

rows.title: Linen garments

The Law & history: make the turban of fine linen

rows.alike: "linen undergarments" (Exodus 28:42; Leviticus 16:4; Ezekiel 44:18), "the linen turban" and "linen turbans", and "linen garments" (Leviticus 16:23; Ezekiel 44:17); in Leviticus 16:23 and Ezekiel 44:19 the garments are taken off and left: "leave them there", "leave them in the holy chambers".
rows.different: Leviticus 16:23 says it of Aaron "before entering the Most Holy Place"; Ezekiel 44:17 adds "they must not wear anything made of wool" and 44:19 "so that they do not transmit holiness to the people with their garments". The asides use "linen garments" of a wager, a trade and finery.

rows.title: No inheritance: the LORD is their inheritance

The Law & history: You will have no inheritance in their land, nor will you have any portion among them. I am your portion and your inheritance among the Israelites.
The Levites will not receive an inheritance among the Israelites.

The LORD, the God of Israel, is their inheritance

Psalms & wisdom: The LORD is my chosen portion and my cup

The Prophets: I am their inheritance. You are to give them no possession in Israel, for I am their possession.

rows.alike: "I am your portion and your inheritance" (Numbers 18:20), "the LORD is his inheritance" (Deuteronomy 10:9), "I am their inheritance" (Ezekiel 44:28), each with a denied share: "no inheritance in their land", "no portion or inheritance among his brothers", "no possession in Israel".
rows.different: Joshua 13:14 names "The food offerings to the LORD" as their inheritance and Joshua 18:7 "the priesthood of the LORD"; Ezekiel 44:28 adds "I am their possession". In the Psalms and Lamentations 3:24 the speaker says it of the speaker's own life: "The LORD is my portion".

rows.title: A tenth to the Levites

The Law & history: I have given to the Levites all the tithes in Israel as an inheritance in return for the work they do

the tithes of grain, new wine, and oil prescribed for the Levites
The Prophets: Bring the full tithe into the storehouse, so that there may be food in My house.
The letters: Even the patriarch Abraham gave him a tenth of the plunder.
the law commands the sons of Levi who become priests to collect a tenth from the people

rows.alike: The Levites "collect the tenth" in Nehemiah 10:38 and Hebrews 7:8, and Hebrews 7:5 says "the law commands the sons of Levi who become priests to collect a tenth"; Numbers 18:21 gives "to the Levites all the tithes in Israel".
rows.different: Numbers 18:26 has the Levites give "a tithe of the tithe"; Malachi 3:10 says "Bring the full tithe into the storehouse" without naming the Levites; Hebrews 7:4-6 and 7:8-9 set the Levites' tenth beside Melchizedek, who "collected a tenth from Abraham", and add "Levi, who collects the tenth, paid the tenth through Abraham".

rows.title: The sons of Levi purified

The Law & history: Take the Levites from among the Israelites and make them ceremonially clean.
Sprinkle them with the water of purification.

All the priests and Levites had purified themselves and were ceremonially clean.

The Prophets: And He will sit as a refiner and purifier of silver; He will purify the sons of Levi and refine them like gold and silver. Then they will present offerings to the LORD in righteousness.

rows.alike: "The Levites purified themselves" (Numbers 8:21), "the priests and Levites had purified themselves" (Ezra 6:20; Nehemiah 12:30), "He will purify the sons of Levi" (Malachi 3:3).
rows.different: In Numbers 8:21, Ezra 6:20 and Nehemiah 12:30 the Levites purify themselves; in Nehemiah 13:30 "I purified the priests and Levites"; Malachi 3:3 speaks of one who "will sit as a refiner and purifier of silver", adds "refine them like gold and silver", and "Then they will present offerings to the LORD in righteousness".

rows.title: Keep charge of the sanctuary

The Law & history: The priests must keep My charge, lest they bear the guilt and die
the Levites who keep charge of the tabernacle of the LORD

rows.alike: "the Levites who keep charge of the tabernacle of the LORD" (Numbers 31:30) and "the priests who keep charge of the temple", "kept charge of My sanctuary" (Ezekiel 40:45; 44:15); Leviticus 22:9 "The priests must keep My charge" and Ezekiel 44:16 "They will keep My charge".
rows.different: Leviticus 22:9 adds "lest they bear the guilt and die"; Ezekiel names "the sons of Zadok" (40:46), sets them against Levites who did "go astray" (48:11), and says "you have not kept charge of My holy things" (44:8). The asides use "keep My charge" of keeping God's "commandments" and "statutes".

rows.title: Show yourself to the priest

The Law & history: he must be brought to Aaron the priest or to one of his sons who is a priest
The priest is to examine the infection on his skin

rows.different: Matthew 8:4 has "offer the gift prescribed by Moses"; Matthew 8:4 and Mark 1:44 add "See that you don't tell anyone" (Luke 5:14: "Do not tell anyone"), and all three have "as a testimony to them"; in Luke 17:14 "as they were on their way, they were cleansed". Leviticus 13:49 says "shown to the priest" of "mildew"; Deuteronomy 24:8 says "follow everything the Levitical priests instruct you".

rows.title: The consecrated bread, lawful only for the priests

The Law & history: It belongs to Aaron and his sons, who are to eat it in a holy place

rows.alike: Mark 2:26 and Luke 6:4 say the consecrated bread is "lawful only for the priests" (Luke: "what is lawful only for the priests to eat"), and Matthew 12:4 "but only for the priests"; Leviticus 24:9 says "It belongs to Aaron and his sons, who are to eat it in a holy place" of "a most holy part of the food offerings to the LORD"; and "the consecrated bread" is the words of 1 Samuel 21:6, Matthew 12:4 and Mark 2:26.
rows.different: 1 Samuel 21:4 names a condition, "provided that the young men have kept themselves from women"; Mark 2:26 adds "During the high priesthood of Abiathar"; Matthew 12:4 says "not lawful for them to eat".

rows.title: The division of Abijah, chosen by lot

rows.alike: Those who serve at the altar eat what is offered: "Every male among the priests may eat of it." (Leviticus 7:6), "The priest who offers it shall eat it" (Leviticus 6:26), "They shall eat the grain offerings, the sin offerings, and the guilt offerings." (Ezekiel 44:29), "those who serve at the altar partake of its offerings" (1 Corinthians 9:13).

rows.title: Once a year

rows.title: For himself and for the people

rows.alike: "the priest will make atonement on their behalf" (Leviticus 4:20) and "high priest in service to God, in order to make atonement for the sins of the people" (Hebrews 2:17).
rows.different: Leviticus most often adds "and he will be forgiven" (4:26; 5:10) and names the offering, "with the ram of the guilt offering" (19:22); in Leviticus 12:8 it ends "she will be clean"; in Numbers 16:47 Aaron "offered the incense and made atonement for the people"; Hebrews 2:17 adds "He had to be made like His brothers in every way".

rows.title: Anointing oil poured on his head

The Law & history: anoint them, ordain them, and consecrate them so that they may serve Me as priests

The priest who is anointed and ordained to succeed his father as high priest

the high priest, who was anointed with the holy oil

Psalms & wisdom: It is like fine oil on the head, running down on the beard, running down Aaron's beard over the collar of his robes.
You anoint my head with oil
never spare the oil for your head
Gospels & Acts: a woman came to Him with an alabaster jar of expensive perfume, which she poured on His head
She broke open the jar and poured it on Jesus' head.

when you fast, anoint your head

rows.alike: "anoint him by pouring it on his head" (Exodus 29:7), "poured some of the anointing oil on Aaron's head" (Leviticus 8:12), "the anointing oil poured on his head" (Leviticus 21:10), and Psalm 133:2 "fine oil on the head, running down on the beard, running down Aaron's beard".
rows.different: Psalm 133:2 is a likeness, "It is like fine oil on the head"; Numbers 35:25 says "anointed with the holy oil"; Leviticus 10:7 and 21:12 give the oil as the reason for a restriction: "the LORD's anointing oil is on you" (10:7), "the consecration of the anointing oil of his God is on him" (21:12). The asides use the words of anointing a king ("I anoint you king", 2 Kings 9:3), of everyday oil ("never spare the oil for your head"), and of a woman who "poured it on Jesus' head" (Mark 14:3).

rows.title: Priests clothed with righteousness and salvation

The Law & history: May Your priests, O LORD God, be clothed with salvation, and may Your godly ones rejoice in goodness.

So a clean turban was placed on his head, and they clothed him
He put on righteousness like a breastplate, and the helmet of salvation on His head

rows.alike: "May Your priests be clothed with righteousness" (Psalm 132:9), "May Your priests, O LORD God, be clothed with salvation" (2 Chronicles 6:41), "I will clothe her priests with salvation" (Psalm 132:16), "He has clothed me with garments of salvation" (Isaiah 61:10).
rows.different: Psalm 132:9 and 2 Chronicles 6:41 are prayers ("May Your priests"), Psalm 132:16 a promise ("I will clothe"); Isaiah 61:10 is said by one who rejoices, "as a bridegroom wears a priestly headdress"; Zechariah 3:4 says "I have removed your iniquity, and I will clothe you with splendid robes". Job 29:14 and Isaiah 59:17 use the words of others: "I put on righteousness", "He put on righteousness like a breastplate".

rows.title: A faithful priest

The Law & history: Then I will raise up for Myself a faithful priest. He will do whatever is in My heart and mind. And I will build for him an enduring house, and he will walk before My anointed one for all time.
The letters: so that He might become a merciful and faithful high priest in service to God

rows.alike: "a faithful priest" (1 Samuel 2:35) and "a merciful and faithful high priest" (Hebrews 2:17); Hebrews 3:1-2 has "high priest" and "He was faithful".
rows.different: 1 Samuel 2:35 adds "I will build for him an enduring house, and he will walk before My anointed one for all time"; Hebrews 2:17 adds "merciful", and Hebrews 3:2 "just as Moses was faithful in all God's house".

rows.title: Aaron's staff that budded

The Law & history: The staff belonging to the man I choose will sprout
Aaron's staff, representing the house of Levi, had sprouted, put forth buds, blossomed, and produced almonds

The letters: Inside the ark were the gold jar of manna, Aaron's staff that had budded, and the stone tablets of the covenant.

rows.alike: Numbers 17:8 "Aaron's staff" that "put forth buds" and Hebrews 9:4 "Aaron's staff that had budded".
rows.different: Numbers 17:5 says "The staff belonging to the man I choose will sprout", and 17:6 has it among twelve staffs, "one for each of the leaders of their tribes"; 17:10 places it "in front of the Testimony, to be kept as a sign for the rebellious"; Hebrews 9:4 places it "Inside the ark" with "the gold jar of manna" and "the stone tablets of the covenant".

rows.title: No one takes this honor upon himself

The Law & history: you are seeking the priesthood as well

Uzziah, you have no right to offer incense to the LORD. Only the priests, the descendants of Aaron, are consecrated to burn incense. Leave the sanctuary, for you have acted unfaithfully; you will not receive honor from the LORD God.
The letters: No one takes this honor upon himself; he must be called by God, just as Aaron was.

rows.alike: Numbers 16:40 and 2 Chronicles 26:18 keep the task for "a descendant of Aaron", "the descendants of Aaron", and Hebrews 5:4 says "he must be called by God, just as Aaron was"; 2 Chronicles 26:18 and Hebrews 5:4 both speak of "honor".
rows.different: Numbers 16:10 and 2 Chronicles 26:18 are said to those who reached for it: "you are seeking the priesthood as well", "you have no right"; Hebrews 5:4 says "No one takes this honor upon himself", and 5:5 of Christ, who "did not take upon Himself the glory of becoming a high priest".

rows.title: A permanent priesthood

The Law & history: The priesthood shall be theirs by a permanent statute.
Their anointing will qualify them for a permanent priesthood throughout their generations.
The letters: there have been many other priests, since death prevented them from continuing in office
But because Jesus lives forever, He has a permanent priesthood.

rows.alike: "a permanent priesthood throughout their generations" (Exodus 40:15) and "He has a permanent priesthood" (Hebrews 7:24); Exodus 29:9 "by a permanent statute".
rows.different: In Exodus it is given by statute and by anointing: "Their anointing will qualify them"; Hebrews 7:24 gives the reason "because Jesus lives forever", and 7:23 says "there have been many other priests, since death prevented them from continuing in office".

rows.title: The LORD has sworn: a priest with an oath

The Law & history: God is not a man, that He should lie, or a son of man, that He should change His mind.
the Glory of Israel does not lie or change His mind
Psalms & wisdom: The LORD has sworn and will not change His mind

rows.alike: Psalm 110:4 and Hebrews 7:21 share "has sworn and will not change His mind" ("The LORD" in the Psalm, "The Lord" in Hebrews).
rows.different: Hebrews 7:20-21 sets this beside "others became priests without an oath", and 7:28 says "the law appoints as high priests men who are weak; but the oath, which came after the law, appointed the Son". Numbers 23:19 and 1 Samuel 15:29 use "change His mind" of other words of God.

rows.title: People presented as an offering

The Law & history: Aaron is to present the Levites before the LORD as a wave offering from the sons of Israel
present them before the LORD as a wave offering

The Prophets: they will bring all your brothers from all the nations as a gift to the LORD

The letters: to be a minister of Christ Jesus to the Gentiles in the priestly service of the gospel of God, so that the Gentiles might become an offering acceptable to God, sanctified by the Holy Spirit

rows.alike: In each, people are what is offered or brought to God: the Levites "as a wave offering" (Numbers 8:11), "all your brothers from all the nations as a gift to the LORD" (Isaiah 66:20), "so that the Gentiles might become an offering acceptable to God" (Romans 15:16).
rows.different: In Numbers it is Aaron who presents "the Levites"; Isaiah 66:20 compares it to how "the Israelites bring an offering in a clean vessel" and 66:21 adds "I will select some of them as priests and Levites"; Romans 15:16 speaks of "a minister of Christ Jesus to the Gentiles in the priestly service of the gospel of God" and an offering "sanctified by the Holy Spirit".
